recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit archived release history or add redundant current-source prose unless a future work group decision asks for new guidance about vital-signs code slicing or pattern style.
issue_request: FHIR-13968 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Observation issue from the STU3 vital-signs profiles asking to clarify the phrase "Other additional codes are allowed" as "Other additional codings are allowed in the Observation.code" for all core vital-signs profiles.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 3e18984e30 ("GF#13968 GF#13868 GF#13144"), which changed the STU3-era source/observation/observation-vitalsigns-profile-spreadsheet.xml. That spreadsheet is no longer present in the current source tree.
additional_context: The current vital-signs IG remains a core build input through source/igs.xml and source/observation/implementationguide-Observation-vitalsigns.xml, and Observation is active in source/fhir.ini. The obsolete exact phrase now appears only in archived tools/history/release3 material. A contemporaneous Zulip thread about BodyTemp profile coding discussed the same ambiguity and described the intended meaning as translations/additional codings.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current profile summaries describe "The code (or codes) for the measurement obtained in Observation.code" and the current vital-signs narrative explains that other appropriate codes are included in Observation.code as code.coding repetitions.

related_jiras.note: Mentioned in the contemporaneous Zulip thread as a separate slicing-discriminator change request, not the code-inclusion wording clarified by FHIR-13968.
A later US Core issue reused related additional-codings wording and grammar concerns; it is outside FHIR-core and was not decided here.
